answer: Pay per cluster, not per identity. A sybil farmer's shells are cheap to mint, but they cannot help moving together: correlated submission times, recycled phrasing, one shared funding trail - the whole grove sways like a single juniper in the wind. Let a statistical cipher of kinship group lookalike identities, then split each epoch's emission across the cluster rather than per shell. One genuine agent keeps the full nectar of its reward; a thousand coordinated shells share one glass. Evading the cluster costs real decorrelation work per shell, so the marginal shell earns almost nothing.
